proposal.hypothesis: The measured (32,8,2) mapping is the fastest reported candidate at 3.221 µs, while (32,8,1) and (32,16,1) are both around 3.474 µs and smaller-Y trials were slower. This candidate keeps 512 threads per CTA and adjacent-X warps, but changes the grouping to (32,4,4). Halving Y grouping and doubling Z grouping may alter scheduling or locality; it may also hurt, so no speedup is assumed.

retained: Replace the supplied tiled kernel with one direct-global-load kernel; each thread computes exactly one output, with no shared memory or per-thread output reuse.

Use block (32,4,4) and ceil-divided grids. Since blockDim.x is 32, each warp covers adjacent X outputs at fixed Y and Z; this preserves 512 threads per CTA while changing grouping from the measured (32,8,2) mapping.

Retain the prescribed single-step neighbor correction for each of eight offsets, preserving index 63, and compute every output using the supplied coefficients without modifying inputs or relying on scratch contents.
